   his dialog answers read 2026-11-17T12:05:56Z; the last wrap's `inputs#I5`): an ignore is admitted for an
   `unmaintained` advisory with no safe upgrade whose crate an upstream dependency brings into the graph, its
   reason written beside it, and every such ignore re-read at each epoch boundary. Viola's own use of chrono
   STAYS — replacing it is not this chunk's. The plan: the ignore entry with its reason and its re-read ground, the
   config comment re-worded so it states both grounds, and no other advisory admitted by the way. The master row
   is the WRAP's: the plan lists it as an expected amendment and edits no master.
4. **The proof that the gate is green is the chunk's own pre-CI run**: `supply-chain` green on the pushed sha, and
   the whole run green. Name it as the operator entry's acceptance. Say also what would turn the gate red again
   (a new advisory id, the same id once a safe upgrade exists if the tool reads that) — the ignore must not be
   wider than this one id.
5. **The untied tail:** the in-test boots of `viola-e2e`'s `tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` and `tests/cli.rs` end
   with their test, killed or not, as the root tests' now do; and a test kills the tied stamping `viola verify` and

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-17-supply-chain-green-and-booted-tests-end · **Version:** viola-0.2.0 · **Generated:** 2026-11-17T13:40:00Z
Two parts, nothing wider than the entry's two carries at `4ef8f4b9` (`inputs#I1` item 1).

**A — the `supply-chain` gate green again.** CI's `supply-chain` job has read red since ci#44077346281 on one error,
RUSTSEC-2026-0543 «chrono is unmaintained», with no patched version. The advisory database moved; no manifest, lock,
deny config or workflow changed (research «Measured», re-derived by `git diff --stat`). The founder widened the rule
himself (relay `chunks/2026-11-17-booted-wrapper-does-not-outlive-its-test/inputs/I5-relay-booted-wrapper-route-answers.md.txt`
items 1 and 2). An ignore is admitted for an `unmaintained` advisory with no safe upgrade whose crate an upstream
dependency brings into the graph. Its reason is written beside it, and every such ignore is re-read at each epoch
boundary. Viola's own chrono use stays. This chunk adds one ignore entry for that one id to `deny.toml` and re-words
the comment above the list so it states both grounds. It admits no other advisory, adds no `skip` or `allow`, and edits
no master. The standing security-plan row for the widened rule is the wrap's (an Expected amendment below). One
`deny.toml` serves every advisory reader. That covers the root graph in CI `supply-chain` and in the weekly
`nightly.yml` job, and the fuzz audits, which read the root config by walking up (measured: three `advisory-not-detected`
warnings today, four with the ignore, exit 0 both times). The `deny-sync.toml` runs read bans only. The proof is the
chunk's own pre-CI run: `supply-chain` green on the pushed sha, and the whole run green.

**B — the rest of v2-37: every booted test process ends with its test.** The in-test boots of viola-e2e's
`tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` (`options`) and `tests/cli.rs` (`booted`) build `BootOptions` with `tied: false`, so their
supervisors would outlive a SIGKILLed test. Both become tied, as `harness_session`'s boots already are.

The tied stamping `viola verify` the last chunk built has no kill witness. The SIGKILL it is tied with could not pass
one. A SIGKILL runs no drop guard, so a killed verify leaves its `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>*` run dirs (cwd
`crates/viola-e2e/` under nextest, outside the root-anchored `.gitignore:19`), its Run A dir under the OS temp dir and
its `ledger/probes/<pid>/`. The security rows leave those to be removed by hand
(`architecture · decision/verify-removes-only-own-dirs`: «SIGKILL, a crash or a failed handler install leave the
folders to be removed by hand»). The four-way removal rule admits no test-side remover of them
(`security-plan · decision/test-removal-own-dirs-only`). So the stamping verify's parent-death signal becomes SIGTERM.
Verify's own stop, installed before any probe dir or child (`src/cmd/verify.rs:142`), then ends its children and removes
only its own dirs, as `contract/verify-stop/signal` states. The supervisor keeps its SIGKILL. A new witness kills a test
mid-stamp and reads that nothing of the verify is left. A census of viola-e2e's own test sources reads that no in-test
boot stays untied. The last chunk's root census walks only the root `tests/` (`tests/cross_killed_test.rs:37-90`).
Leaned SIGTERM per those two rows and `inputs#I1` item 5 («reads that nothing of it is left»). It is a technical call
inside test-only harness code, crossing no product boundary.

1. **`deny.toml` — the one ignore and both grounds.**
   - In `[advisories]`, add `{ id = "RUSTSEC-2026-0543", reason = "…" }` to the `ignore` list beside the three rmcp
     entries, which stay as they are. Its reason states four things: chrono is unmaintained with no safe upgrade;
     `rmcp 3.4.1` and `schemars 1.2.2` bring it in through viola-mcp, beside viola's and viola-state's own use; it is
     admitted under the founder's unmaintained-upstream ground of 2026-11-17; and it is re-read at each epoch
     boundary.
   - Re-word the comment above the list (lines 11–12) so it states both grounds. First: an advisory confined to an rmcp
     feature viola's graph leaves off, standing while rmcp stays below 3.5 (the Critical CVE response). Second: an
     `unmaintained` advisory with no safe upgrade whose crate an upstream dependency brings into the graph, its reason
     beside it, re-read at each epoch boundary.
   - The comment and the reason name no host path and quote no upstream text.
   - Nothing else in the file moves: the bans, the licences, the sources and `[graph]` stay.

2. **`crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs` — the stamping verify tied by SIGTERM.**
   - `tie_to_caller` takes the parent-death signal as a parameter. Its two callers (research «Graph impact»: `stamp` at
     `:301`, `spawn_supervisor` at `:357`) pass SIGTERM and SIGKILL respectively.
   - Its doc comment, the `tied` field's doc comment and `spawn_supervisor`'s doc comment say which child takes which
     signal and why: verify's stop removes its own dirs, which a SIGKILL never would.
   - The `getppid` check and `_exit(1)` stay as they are.

3. **`crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` — `options()` boots tied:** `tied: true` at line 28. Every boot of
   the file goes through `options()`, four of them by struct update (`:213`, `:329`, `:358`, `:380`), so all are tied.
   The `Booted` guard and its keep rule stay. Keeps tests S2.

4. **`crates/viola-e2e/tests/cli.rs` — `booted()` boots tied:** `tied: true` at line 176. The `Booted` guard stays.
   Keeps tests S2.

5. **`crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_tied.rs` — the stamped victim and its witness**
   (`killed_test_leaves_no_stamping_verify`). Keeps tests S1–S4, arch S1–S2, security S1–S2 and S4, and obs S1–S2.
   - **The victim.** A second victim entry, `harness_stamped_victim_entry`, behind the same `HARNESS_TIED_TEST_CHILD`
     marker. It returns at once without the marker. With it, it opens a STAMPED one-instance `harness_session`
     (`unstamped: false`), labelled `stamped`, then parks.
   - **Spawning it.** The witness spawns it through the existing `spawn_victim` form, tied to the witness by
     `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` with the `getppid` check, `--exact harness_stamped_victim_entry`.
   - **Finding the verify.** The witness reads its own victim's tree by pid and start time (`recorded_tree`). It waits,
     bounded by `WITHIN` (12 s), for a descendant that is the session's `viola` running `verify`, read from
     `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, which has at least one child of its own.
   - **What it records, then the kill.** It records that verify's pid and start time, its cwd (`/proc/<pid>/cwd`), its
     `--home` value, and every descendant with its start time and cwd. Only then does it SIGKILL the victim and reap it.
   - **Processes gone.** It waits, through `gone_within`, until the verify and every descendant it recorded are gone by
     pid and start time within `WITHIN`. At the deadline it kills only those recorded survivors and panics naming them.
   - **Dirs gone.** It reads these paths absent: `<verify cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>`, `-dialogs`, `-plan` and
     `-resume`; `<home>/ledger/probes/<pid>`; and every recorded descendant cwd whose path holds a `viola-verify-`
     component, which is Run A's OS-temp dir when the kill lands in Run A.
   - **The victim's leftovers.** The witness then removes what the killed boot itself left and no `cleanup` reaches,
     since no session record was written. Two dirs: the `viola-session-*` parent of `<home>`, taken only when its name
     opens `viola-session-` and its parent is `Workspace::e2e_home()` (the check `cleanup`'s `remove_session_home`
     makes); and `ws.session_dir("harness_tied-stamped-<victim pid>")`. Both are harness-made dirs taken by their session
     name, the rule's third way. The test removes nothing else.

6. **`crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_tied.rs` — the viola-e2e boot census**
   (`viola_e2e_census_finds_no_untied_boot`).
   - It reads every `.rs` file under `crates/viola-e2e/tests/`, recursively and named or not. The file's module comment
     carries the `andromeda:walks-tree` token.
   - It counts, in code only (line comments and string literals cut first, as `untied_spawns` does at
     `tests/cross_killed_test.rs:37-56`), every spelling that sets a boot's `tied` to anything but `true`: a `tied:`
     field whose value is not the literal `true`, at any spacing. It also counts every `BootOptions::for_cli(` call,
     the builder that leaves the supervisor untied.
   - A planted text first proves the counter: two counted sites, plus a commented and a string-literal spelling not
     counted.
   - It asserts the walk reaches `harness_tied.rs` and `harness_lifecycle.rs`, then asserts zero hits across the files.
   - It leaves `src/` alone. The CLI builder and the unit tests stand there by contract (research «Sweeps»: 8
     no-change hits).

7. **Order.** Steps 1–4 are independent. Step 5 needs step 2, and its control (below) reads red without it. Step 6
   needs steps 3 and 4. Implement writes steps 5 and 6 red-before-green: run each new case against the tree without
   steps 2–4 once, then land those steps.
- none
- `deny.toml` — the RUSTSEC-2026-0543 ignore entry and the two-ground comment (step 1)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs` — `tie_to_caller`'s signal parameter; SIGTERM for the stamping verify (step 2)
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_lifecycle.rs` — `options()` tied (step 3)
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/cli.rs` — `booted()` tied (step 4)
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_tied.rs` — the stamped victim, its kill witness and the boot census (steps 5, 6)

**No smoke entry, no live leg, no mutation run.** The product binary is unchanged, so there is no `smoke` entry. The
test-plan declares no boot-smoke path list. The harness `boot` changes only the stamping verify's parent-death signal,
and its CLI arm (`for_cli`, untied) is unchanged. No live `claude` start and no mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 6).

**Bounds and sockets.** Every wait this chunk adds goes through `WITHIN` (12 s), below the mutants kill (15 s), the
20 s lint and cargo-mutants' 20 s floor (`tests/contract_lints.rs` `test_deadlines_sit_below_the_nextest_kill_line`,
entry 11). No test socket is added; a booted session's sockets stay in the product's per-user directory as today.

**Why the run needs CI.** The acceptance needs CI (`inputs#I1` item 4), so the operator pass carries pre-push,
hygiene, push and the CI read. `deny.toml` is no Rust source, and nothing here is OS-conditional (Linux only, one
`ubuntu-latest` leg).

**Filters.** Every filter is checked to select at least one test. Entries 8 and 9 select today's cases (harness_tied:
`killed_test_leaves_no_harness_session`; harness_lifecycle and viola-e2e's `cli`: their booted cases). Entry 10
selects the MCP binaries' `harness_session` boots.
**What would turn each predicate red:**

- **Entry 3.** It reads red on any new advisory against the root graph: an `unmaintained`, `unsound` or vulnerability
  id, or a yanked crate.
- **Entry 4.** It reads red on the same against the fuzz graph.
- **Entry 5.** It reads red when the ignore list gains or loses any id. So the ignore is no wider than this one id.

- **RUSTSEC-2026-0543 itself.** cargo-deny's ignore entry is keyed on the id alone; this chunk writes its only fields,
  `id` and `reason`. So the same id turns no reader red once a safe upgrade exists. A withdrawn advisory reads
  `advisory-not-detected`, a warning (measured on cargo-deny 0.20.2: four such warnings, exit 0). The founder's re-read
  at each epoch boundary is the control for a safe upgrade. That this cargo-deny ignores an id whatever its patched
  versions is read from the config's field set and not measured; it is recorded as an owed reading below.

**Controls.** Each is implement's one-shot `gate.py control`, never an entry, fired with `--timeout 600` on the entry
filtered to its own case. 600 s covers the control clone's cold build of the filtered binary: the last chunk read its
firings at 4.4–47.56 s, `doc:2026-11-17-booted-wrapper-does-not-outlive-its-test/plan` §Test Commands. «Holds» means
the named case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line; a `timeout` reading reads the control NOT held.

- `vfy-term` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs`: the SIGTERM `stamp` passes to `tie_to_caller` replaced by
  SIGKILL, today's signal. Case `killed_test_leaves_no_stamping_verify`, on entry 8. It holds when the case fails on its
  dir read: a SIGKILLed verify leaves its run dirs.

- `vfy-tie` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs`: `stamp`'s `tie_to_caller` call removed. Case
  `killed_test_leaves_no_stamping_verify`, on entry 8. It holds when the case fails on its process read; `gone_within`'s
  failure path kills the recorded survivors, so the firing leaves nothing running.

- `e2e-census` — `crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_lifecycle.rs`: `options()`'s `tied: true` reverted to `tied: false`.
  Case `viola_e2e_census_finds_no_untied_boot`, on entry 8.

## 2026-11-17-supply-chain-green-and-booted-tests-end — the advisory rule widened, ratified by the founder
**Section:** Dependency Security
**Change:** decision/advisory-ignore-grounds and decision/advisory-ignore-list stand as the widened advisory rule: an ignore stands on the Critical CVE response for a disabled feature, or on an unmaintained advisory with no safe upgrade whose crate an upstream dependency brings into the graph, its reason beside it, every such ignore re-read at each epoch boundary; RUSTSEC-2026-0543 (chrono) the first id on the second ground; viola's own chrono use stays.
**Why:** A boundary widening ratified by the founder's own dialog answer of 2026-11-17, relayed verbatim by the overseer at the previous wrap (its inputs#I5, item 1); the wrap's answer card confirm is the overseer's, delegate the overseer, 2026-11-17, inputs#I4, PROVISIONAL until his own word in the batch at the Epoch 4 boundary. The re-read at each epoch boundary is the second ground's only control: whether cargo-deny keeps ignoring an id once a safe upgrade exists is unmeasured.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-17T14-02-45Z-wrap/

- **Audit tool:** `cargo deny check` (>=0.20.2: advisories, bans, licences — `allow` exactly MIT, Apache-2.0, Zlib, Unicode-3.0, `0BSD` only as the per-crate `[[licenses.exceptions]]` for interprocess's `doctest-file` (the one 0BSD crate in the Linux graph), a new exception needs a Decisions Log entry — sources — crates.io only; the advisory ignore list holds exactly RUSTSEC-2026-0457, RUSTSEC-2026-0461 and RUSTSEC-2026-0462, each in an rmcp feature banned or off in the release graph, its reason naming it, standing until rmcp leaves its below-3.5 range, and RUSTSEC-2026-0543, chrono unmaintained with no safe upgrade, on the unmaintained-upstream ground, re-read at each epoch boundary; portable-pty pinned `=0.9.0`)); the tokio ban is `deny-sync.toml`, run per sync crate as sole root over the five crates of `scripts/sync-crates.txt`, and for `viola-channel` (its Tokio client behind its `tokio` feature) the `cargo tree` form `scripts/channel-tokio-free.sh` (no `tokio v` line without the feature); `scripts/deny-probes.sh` proves every ban fires; weekly `cargo deny check advisories` in `nightly.yml` over the root and fuzz lockfiles; `zizmor` on workflows. Never widen an ignore, add a `skip`/`allow` or silence zizmor to reach green; an ignore is admitted on two grounds only, each with its reason beside it: the Critical CVE response (within 7 days of an advisory confined to a disabled feature, an ignore entry whose reason names that feature), or an unmaintained advisory with no safe upgrade whose crate an upstream dependency brings into the graph, re-read at every epoch boundary (an advisory against an enabled feature: bump the crate within 7 days).

- **E2E:** `crates/viola-e2e/tests/{path<N>,mcp,cross}_<topic>.rs` (rmcp client; a numbered Path binary is named `path<N>_<topic>.rs`; no test boots a harness session untied: an in-test session ties its supervisor to the test thread by parent-death SIGKILL and its stamping `viola verify` by SIGTERM, and the census `viola_e2e_census_finds_no_untied_boot`, read red on a planted untied boot first, finds every in-test boot tied) on `ubuntu-latest`, CI's one leg, plus the root package's numbered sync Path binaries (`tests/path1_run_start.rs`, `[[test]]` `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`) and its `cross_` binary (`tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`, sync, `[[test]]` `required-features = ["fake-agent"]`), and its `contract_` binary `tests/contract_os_gated_tests.rs` (auto-discovered, no `[[test]]` table; every OS-gated test function and gated file under `tests/` and `crates/*/tests/` a `GATES` row with its reason, an unnamed or stale gate failing the run, and a gate whose predicate names `windows` or `target_os = "macos"` a fault even when a row names it; the census walks only files directly under `tests/` and `crates/*/tests/`, so an integration binary split into a module directory keeps every gated case and its gated helpers in its root file); both homes report in the E2E layer (`run --e2e`, suite `nextest-e2e`), whose regex is `^(path[0-9]*|tui|mcp|cross|chaos|contract)_`.

- `<subject>_<condition>_<expected>`; critical paths `path<N>_<slug>`; rstest case labels readable (`#[case::esc_refused]`; `viola-e2e` carries no `[dev-dependencies]`, so its table-driven cases are a labelled case table of `(label, …)` rows in one `#[test]`, each assertion naming its label; `viola-core` carries no rstest dev-dependency either, so its table-driven cases are literal tables in one `#[test]`, e.g. `dialog_hold_takes_whole_seconds_from_sixty_to_thirty_six_hundred`; and a shared helper taken by path keeps its own cases, which run in every taker, as a labelled table in one test).

- A multi-surface path asserts every surface it lists; a lower-layer case (parser, refusal order, threshold, clock) belongs in unit tests, not E2E. A kill witness for a tied stamping verify (`killed_test_leaves_no_stamping_verify`) waits until verify holds a child inside a viola-verify run dir, asserts an owned dir stood at the kill, and reads the stamp's absence besides processes and dirs: an untied verify orphaned by the kill finishes inside the wait bound and removes its own dirs.

- No nested `cargo run` inside nextest: tests use `viola_e2e::harness::session::harness_session(test, label, opts) -> HarnessSession` (a plain function and drop guard, never an rstest fixture; the library `boot` spawns the `supervise` process from the given binary dir, tying it to the test thread by a parent-death SIGKILL and its stamping `viola verify` by a parent-death SIGTERM; the session is stamped unless `SessionOptions::unstamped`, default false, the in-test form of `boot --unstamped`) or the rstest chain `home → fake_agent_path → stamped_home → booted_wrapper`. No viola-e2e test boots a session untied: `viola_e2e_census_finds_no_untied_boot` finds every in-test boot in viola-e2e's test sources tied, read red on a planted untied boot first.

title: A booted wrapper does not outlive its test

record.title: A booted wrapper does not outlive its test
record.requirement: a wrapper a test boots, and the agent under it, end when that test ends, whether the test passes, fails, times out or is killed, so no booted wrapper or fake agent is left running after a test run
record.observed_gap: On 2026-11-17 a mutation run killed tests at their timeout and five mutant-build wrappers stayed alive, each near 99 % of a core for 5 h 50 min, their fake agents with them; no test-side code ends a booted wrapper when its test is killed.

verification.acceptance: After a test process that booted a wrapper on pipes, by a direct spawn, under an outer PTY, frozen under an outer PTY, or under an in-test harness session is SIGKILLed mid-run, every process of that test's recorded tree (the wrapper, its fake agent, the supervisor) is gone by pid and start time within WITHIN (killed_test_leaves_no_{piped,direct,outer_pty,frozen}_wrapper in tests/cross_killed_test.rs, killed_test_leaves_no_harness_session in crates/viola-e2e/tests/harness_tied.rs); a test that panics leaves none (panicked_test_leaves_no_piped_wrapper); no root test spawns viola outside tests/support/tied.rs (cross_killed_test_census_finds_no_untied_viola_spawn); a test timed out is one the runner kills, the case the witnesses drive, and a test that passes or fails ends its wrapper through the existing Drop guards.
